reason: E1 supports the general capability of laser cladding for TC4, and E2 provides direct evidence that TiAlCu/NbC composite coatings on TC4 increase hardness and wear resistance, accurately matching the key premises. However, the specific claim of 35–50% hardness increase and 40–50% wear rate reduction is an overstatement not directly supported by the cited values (e.g., 47.8% wear rate reduction in a different system).
premises: Laser cladding can produce dense, metallurgically bonded coatings on TC4
TiAl-based coatings are compatible with TC4 and can improve its surface properties
Adding Cu to a TiAl coating increases hardness and wear resistance
Incorporating NbC or TiC forms hard ceramic phases in situ that enhance hardness
The combined effect of Cu and ceramic reinforcements yields substantial hardness and wear rate improvements
